servers.instructions:
# Clinic administration with Veterical

This skill drives the hosted Veterical MCP connector. The user must connect
Veterical and authorize an account that can access the intended organization.
If authorization fails, ask the user to connect or reauthorize; never guess an
identifier or retry with a different tenant.

## Hard privacy, financial and clinical boundary

This connector is administrative-only. It intentionally does not expose:

- animal/patient or owner/client identities, records, contact details or
  record counts;
- individual appointment records, identifiers, statuses, animal/owner links
  or exact booked times;
- diagnoses, treatments, procedure names/descriptions, prescriptions,
  vaccinations, reminders, images or notes;
- provider identifiers, contacts, roles, credentials or organization
  internals;
- transaction identifiers/dates, animal or owner linkage, line items,
  discounts, payment methods, card/bank information or processor identifiers;
  or
- tools that create, update, book, message, cancel, charge, refund, transfer or
  delete anything.

Never ask the user to paste excluded personal or clinical data into chat,
infer it from aggregate counts, or imply that another tool can approximate a
missing capability. The connector does not diagnose, triage, prescribe,
recommend treatment, determine urgency or make any medical decision. It cannot
move funds.

Bookable availability is unassigned clinic capacity inside the clinic's own
online-booking window. Numeric catalog data is administrative configuration,
not evidence that an animal received or should receive a treatment. Patient
and appointment numbers in subscription results are plan caps, not record
counts.

## Available tools

| Tool                          | Use it when someone asks…                                                     |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list_clinics`                | which clinics they manage; also resolves the clinic ID every other tool needs |
| `get_clinic`                  | about one clinic's currency, language or timezone                             |
| `get_clinic_availability`     | when there are free online-booking slots (up to 14 days with openings)        |
| `list_clinic_providers`       | which vets, nurses or assistants can be booked (up to 100 display names)      |
| `get_clinic_schedule_summary` | how busy each UTC day is (appointment counts, at most 31 days)                |
| `list_calendar_events`        | when the clinic is closed or time is blocked (holidays, vacations, meetings)  |
| `list_procedures`             | about the catalog's price range (rows carry no treatment names)               |
| `list_payments`               | how much was taken in, by currency and payment status, one page at a time     |
| `list_subscriptions`          | which plan the clinic is on and its plan caps                                 |
| `show_clinic_overview`        | for a one-card overview of one clinic                                         |

Every tool is read-only. There is no operation for animal/owner lookup,
individual appointment access, booking, rescheduling, cancellation, messaging,
clinical-record access, diagnosis, treatment, payment execution or funds
movement.

## Identifiers and cursors

Never guess a clinic ID. Start with `list_clinics`, choose the clinic matching
the user's request and reuse its returned 24-character lowercase hexadecimal
ID. If several clinics match, ask which one they mean. A cross-organization ID
fails closed.

Tools returning `nextCursor` use opaque cursors. Reuse a cursor only with the
same clinic, date range and limit that produced it. Start a new listing when a
filter changes. Never inspect, edit or manufacture a cursor.

Counts marked `+` are lower bounds from bounded reads. Do not describe them as
complete totals. Payment groups summarize one bounded page; follow the cursor
only if the user needs subsequent pages, and do not combine pages without
clearly stating what was added.

## Administrative overview workflow

When the user wants a broad snapshot:

1. Call `list_clinics`.
2. Resolve the intended clinic without guessing.
3. Call `show_clinic_overview` with that clinic ID.
4. Interpret only safe clinic metadata, aggregate next-seven-day schedule,
   provider/availability counts and numeric catalog previews.

The card does not identify an appointment, owner, animal, provider record or
procedure label. Never infer one.

## Schedule and capacity workflow

For workload over a period:

1. Resolve the clinic with `list_clinics`.
2. Call `get_clinic_schedule_summary` with ISO 8601 start/end values. Omit
   both for the default seven-day range. Never request more than 31 days.
3. Report only the aggregate count and UTC day rows. Counts include canceled
   appointments; say so when describing workload.
4. Use `get_clinic_availability` separately for open capacity and
   `list_clinic_providers` for display names.

Schedule summaries deliberately omit individual records and times. Do not try
to reconstruct them by comparing availability, provider or calendar output.

## Calendar and numeric catalog workflow

Use `list_calendar_events` for closures, meetings, courses, days off and other
non-appointment blocks. It exposes time, all-day state, scope, effect and type.
Titles, notes, IDs and staff references are unavailable. Do not infer a reason
or person from a block.

Use `list_procedures` for numeric price/duration/edit-time configuration at a
resolved clinic. Names and descriptions are intentionally absent. Never label
a row, map it to an animal, or describe it as a diagnosis, treatment history
or care recommendation.

## Payment aggregates and entitlements

Use `list_payments` only for operational amount/count totals grouped by
currency and status. State that totals cover the bounded page reported by the
tool. Never claim access to a transaction, payment method, processor account
or settlement, and never imply that Claude can authorize, capture, refund or
transfer money.

Use `list_subscriptions` for plan status, billing frequency and configuration
caps. It contains no billed amount or processor customer/subscription record.
Do not interpret patient or appointment caps as actual record counts.

## Unsupported requests

For an animal, owner, individual-appointment or clinical request, state that
the public connector cannot access the requested data. For a write request,
state that every tool is read-only. For payment execution or processor data,
state that only aggregate operational totals are available. For diagnosis,
urgency, medication or treatment advice, do not invoke Veterical as a clinical
authority; follow current host safety guidance and make clear that the
connector provides no medical decision.

## Clinic sidebar

Use `open_veterical` when the user asks to open Veterical or browse their clinics. Select an owned clinic for aggregate schedules, booking capacity and numeric catalog prices and durations. The selection supplies clinic context to the assistant. Every view is read-only and excludes animal, owner and clinical records. Counts marked “At least” are lower bounds.

tools.name: list_clinics
tools.title: List your vet clinics
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to list veterinary clinics accessible to the connected Veterical account and retrieve their identifiers for subsequent administrative reads. Returns each clinic's id, name, currency, default language and timezone, 20 per page by default. Not for finding a pet, owner or appointment.

limit.description: Clinics per page, from 1 to 100; defaults to 20

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous page of this listing; absent for the first page

clinics.description: Clinics in the signed-in organization, administrative metadata only. Animal, owner, appointment and clinical records are never returned.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page; null on the last page

tools.name: get_clinic
tools.title: Get vet clinic details
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to read the name, currency, language, timezone and edit time of one Veterical clinic selected by its identifier. Returns the clinic's name, currency, default language, timezone and last edit time; an id outside the organization returns not-found. Not for free appointment slots.

clinic.description: Administrative clinic metadata only; opening hours, staff, animal, owner and appointment data are not included. Null when not found.

tools.name: get_clinic_availability
tools.title: Summarize clinic booking capacity
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to summarize unassigned online-booking capacity for one Veterical clinic as daily slot counts and first/last slot times. Returns the open online-booking slots per day for one clinic: how many, plus the first start and last end time. Covers the next days that have openings, up to 14 days and 100 slots (no pet, owner or medical data). Not for booking an appointment.

slotCountIsLowerBound.description: True when more open slots exist beyond the 14-day, 100-slot cap

days.description: One row per day that has open online-booking slots, in date order. Unassigned capacity only; appointments, animals, owners, staff and clinical data are never included.

tools.name: list_clinic_providers
tools.title: List bookable vets and staff
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to list the display names of staff offered by one Veterical clinic for online booking. Returns up to 100 staff display names for one clinic (no contact details, roles or pet data). Not for staff days off or vacations.

providers.description: Display names of staff with a doctor, nurse or assistant role. Staff identifiers, contact details, roles, colors, avatars and all animal or clinical data are excluded.

tools.name: get_clinic_schedule_summary
tools.title: Count appointments per day
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to count scheduled records by UTC day for one Veterical clinic and a bounded date range, including canceled records. Returns appointment counts per UTC day for one clinic, canceled ones included, for the next 7 days by default and at most 31 days; counting stops at 100. Not for seeing individual appointments, pets or owners.

startTime.description: Start of the range as an ISO 8601 date-time; defaults to now

endTime.description: End of the range as an ISO 8601 date-time, after startTime and at most 31 days later; defaults to 7 days after the start

appointmentCountIsLowerBound.description: True when more than 100 appointments fall in the range

days.description: One row per UTC day that has appointments, canceled ones included. Aggregate counts only: appointment identifiers and times, animals, owners, diagnoses, treatments, reminders and notes are never returned.

tools.name: list_calendar_events
tools.title: List closures, holidays and blocked time
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to list non-appointment calendar blocks and additional opening periods for a Veterical clinic. Returns each block or extra opening with start, end, all-day flag, scope (clinic, staff or room) and type, without titles, notes or names. Not for appointments.

clinicId.description: Only this clinic (24 lowercase hexadecimal characters); every clinic when absent

startTime.description: Only blocks starting at or after this ISO 8601 date-time

endTime.description: Only blocks ending before this ISO 8601 date-time

limit.description: Blocks per page, from 1 to 100; defaults to 20

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous page with the same filters; absent for the first page

annotations.title: List closures, holidays and blocked time

scope.description: CLINIC: the whole clinic; PROVIDER: one or more staff; SEAT: one room

effect.description: BLOCK removes bookable time; OPEN adds hours on a normally closed time

type.description: Label such as COURSE, MEETING, VACATION, SICK, HOLIDAY, MAINTENANCE or OTHER

calendarEvents.description: Non-appointment calendar blocks, earliest first. Event identifiers, clinic or staff references, titles, notes, owner or animal linkage and clinical fields are never returned.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page; null on the last page

tools.name: list_procedures
tools.title: List numeric clinic catalog rows
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to read anonymous numeric catalog rows from a Veterical clinic to inspect configured prices, durations and edit times. Returns price, duration where recorded and last edit time per catalog row, without treatment names. Not for the price of a specific named treatment.

limit.description: Catalog rows per page, from 1 to 100; defaults to 50

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous page with the same filters; absent for the first page

duration.description: Configured duration, or null when none was recorded

procedures.description: Numeric catalog rows, most recently edited first. Names, descriptions, identifiers, patient-linked treatments, diagnoses, notes, reminders and every other free-text or clinical field are excluded.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page; null on the last page

tools.name: list_payments
tools.title: Summarize a page of payment totals
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to aggregate one bounded page of recorded Veterical payments by currency and status; this is not a full revenue or settlement report. Returns totals and counts by currency and status for one page of payments, newest first (20 by default), with a cursor for the rest (no client, pet or card data). Not for refunds or charging a client.

clinicId.description: Only this clinic (24 lowercase hexadecimal characters); every clinic when absent

startTime.description: Only payments dated at or after this ISO 8601 date-time

endTime.description: Only payments dated before this ISO 8601 date-time

limit.description: Payments to summarize in this page, from 1 to 100; defaults to 20

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous page with the same filters; absent for the first page

annotations.title: Summarize a page of payment totals

recordsSummarized.description: How many payment records this page summarized

moreRecordsAvailable.description: True when older payments exist beyond this page

totals.description: One row per currency and status within this page only. Transaction identifiers and dates, animal or owner linkage, line items, discounts, payment methods, card or bank data and processor identifiers are never returned.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page; null on the last page

tools.name: list_subscriptions
tools.title: Check Veterical plan and limits
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to read the subscription plan, status, billing frequency and configured capacity limits for a Veterical clinic. Returns plan name, status, billing frequency and plan caps per subscription; caps are limits, not usage. Not for invoices or amounts billed.

clinicId.description: Only this clinic (24 lowercase hexadecimal characters); every clinic when absent

limit.description: Subscriptions per page, from 1 to 100; defaults to 20

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous page with the same filters; absent for the first page

limits.description: Plan caps, not record counts; null when the subscription carries no cap

subscriptions.description: Plan entitlements, newest first. Subscription or customer ids, billed amounts, payment methods, invoices and every processor field are excluded.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page; null on the last page

tools.name: show_clinic_overview
tools.title: Show vet clinic overview
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to render a read-only administrative overview for one Veterical clinic selected by its identifier. Returns an overview card with the clinic's details, appointment counts for the next 7 days, how many staff can be booked, open online-booking slots and up to 12 catalog prices (no pet, owner or medical data). Not for a single appointment.

clinic.description: Administrative clinic metadata; null when the clinic was not found. The overview never includes individual appointments, animal or owner records, diagnoses, treatments, reminders, notes, transaction details or other clinical or personal data.

tools.name: open_veterical
tools.title: Veterical Veterinary Software
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to open the Veterical clinic-selection sidebar when the user requests an interactive clinic browser. Returns up to 100 clinics to start from (no pet, owner, appointment or clinical data). Not for booking appointments, editing records or medical decisions.

resources.name: veterical-clinic-overview
resources.description: An inline Veterical view that presents aggregate, tenant-scoped clinic operations.

resources.name: veterical-schedule-summary
resources.description: An inline Veterical view for non-identifying, tenant-scoped administrative schedule counts.

resources.name: clinic-administration
resources.title: clinic-administration skill
resources.description: Review a Veterical clinic's safe administrative configuration and capacity — clinic metadata, bookable capacity summaries, provider display names, aggregate schedules, non-text calendar blocks, numeric catalog data, payment aggregates and plan entitlements. Use when asked about a vet clinic's free appointment slots, how busy each day is, closures and blocked time, bookable staff, catalog prices, payment totals or plan limits through the Veterical connector. Never use for animal or owner records, individual appointments, clinical information, payment execution, medical advice, diagnosis, triage, prescribing or treatment decisions.

# Veterical CLI

`veterical` reads and manages the data on
[app.veterical.com](https://app.veterical.com) through the Veterical REST API:
clients, patients, appointments, invoices, payments and vaccination records —
the same records the clinic dashboard shows.

Two of the nouns are easy to mix up. A **client** is the human who owns the
animal. A **patient** is the animal itself. A patient therefore belongs to a
client, and an appointment usually names both.

Run it as `veterical` when installed globally (`npm install -g veterical`) or
as `npx veterical` otherwise. `veterical --help` and
`veterical <command> --help` are accurate and self-sufficient;
`veterical schema` prints the whole command tree as JSON — prefer those over
memory when unsure of a flag. `veterical skills list` names the guides bundled
with the installed version, and `veterical skills get veterical` prints the
copy of this guide matching it.

## Setup

No account yet? Create one without leaving the terminal — the generated
password prints exactly once, the first clinic is seeded for you, and the
session is stored so every other command works immediately:

```bash
veterical signup --email vet@example.com --json
```

```bash
veterical login                # interactive: browser, another device or API key
veterical login --browser      # opens app.veterical.com/cli; stores a session
veterical login --device       # approve from a phone or another computer; stores a session
veterical login --with-key     # masked prompt for an API key secret
veterical logout               # clears everything stored in ~/.veterical/
```

Three ways in, all stored in `~/.veterical/`:

- **Browser** — `veterical login --browser` opens
  [app.veterical.com](https://app.veterical.com) to sign in and stores a token
  session, refreshed automatically. A browser session is organization-wide, so
  it can reach every clinic of the organization — and must name a clinic on
  writes.
- **Another device** — `veterical login --device` prints a link such as
  `https://app.veterical.com/cli?code=WDJB-MJHT`, a QR code and a one-time code,
  then waits up to ten minutes for someone signed in to Veterical to approve it
  on a phone or computer, and stores the same token session as the browser
  login. It needs neither a browser on this machine nor a terminal: when you run
  it for someone, give them the link and the code.
- **API key** — an administrator of the organization creates a key in the
  dashboard, on the clinic page under **API keys**. The secret is shown once,
  at creation. `veterical login --with-key` prompts for it interactively,
  masked — never pass it as a command argument and never echo it, so it stays
  out of shell history and transcripts. A key belongs to exactly one clinic,
  which is then implied on every call.

Headless agents can skip logging in entirely: export
`VETERICAL_API_KEY=<key secret>` and every command authenticates with it at
request time. When several credentials exist the precedence is: stored browser
session, then stored key, then the environment variable — a stored login always
wins over an exported key.

Without a terminal nothing hangs and no browser is ever opened: `login` exits 1
immediately with instructions on stderr, and commands run with no credentials
fail the same way. A `401` ending in "Not logged in?" means log in again, or
export `VETERICAL_API_KEY`, then retry.

### Scopes

An API key carries per-resource scopes: `clients:read`, `clients:write`,
`patients:read`, `patients:write`, `appointments:read`, `appointments:write`,
`invoices:read`, `invoices:write`, `payments:read`, `payments:write`,
`vaccinations:read`, `vaccinations:write`. New keys start read-only. A `403`
naming a missing scope is a permissions gap, not a bug — an administrator
widens the key in the dashboard. Requests are rate limited per key; a `429`
means back off, not retry-loop. A browser login carries the user's own
permissions instead of key scopes.

Users, roles, invites, clinics, quotes, documents, templates, preferences,
printers and subscriptions are deliberately outside the key vocabulary and
cannot be reached with an API key at all.

## Where to start

| You want                             | Run                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| The owners on file                   | `veterical clients list`                   |
| Find an owner by email               | `veterical clients list --email <email>`   |
| The animals on file                  | `veterical patients list`                  |
| A calendar window                    | `veterical appointments list --startTime … --endTime …` |
| Billing for one animal               | `veterical invoices list --patientId <id>` |
| Recorded payments                    | `veterical payments list`                  |
| Vaccination history and recalls      | `veterical vaccinations list --patientId <id>` |
| One record, formatted                | `veterical clients read <id>` (or the patients / appointments / invoices / payments / vaccinations equivalent) |
| The command tree as JSON             | `veterical schema` (or `veterical schema clients list` for one subtree) |

Ids are Veterical record ids — get them from the `list` commands, never guess
them. A record owned by another clinic or organization responds `404`,
indistinguishable from a missing one; that is tenant isolation, not an error to
work around.

## Clients — the animal owners

```bash
veterical clients list                              # --json for raw output
veterical clients list --clinicId <clinicId>        # one clinic only
veterical clients list --email jane@example.com     # exact-email lookup
veterical clients list --ids <id1,id2>              # fetch specific ids
veterical clients list --fields name,email,phone    # project fields
veterical clients get <clientId>
veterical clients read <clientId>
veterical clients add --name "Jane Fonda" --email jane@example.com \
  --phone 5551234567 --clinicId <clinicId>
veterical clients update <clientId> --phone 5559876543
veterical clients update <clientId> --body '{"language":"it"}'
veterical clients delete <clientId...>              # one or more ids — permanent
```

`--email` on list is an exact match, not a search. `add` is not idempotent —
list first and check the owner does not already exist before creating one.

## Patients — the animals

```bash
veterical patients list                             # --clinicId, --ids, --fields
veterical patients get <patientId>
veterical patients read <patientId>
veterical patients add --name Luna --clientId <clientId> --species dog \
  --breed "Labrador Retriever" --sex female --dateOfBirth 2021-04-18 \
  --clinicId <clinicId>
veterical patients update <patientId> --microchip 981000000000000
veterical patients delete <patientId...>            # one or more ids — permanent
```

Register an animal against the `clientId` of the owner who brought it in; look
that owner up first rather than creating a duplicate.

## Appointments

```bash
veterical appointments list                         # --clinicId, --clientId, --patientId
veterical appointments list --startTime 2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z \
  --endTime 2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z                # ISO-8601 window
veterical appointments list --sortField startTime --sortDirection ASC -n 50
veterical appointments get <appointmentId>
veterical appointments read <appointmentId>
veterical appointments add --startTime 2026-08-10T14:00:00.000Z \
  --endTime 2026-08-10T14:30:00.000Z --clientId <clientId> \
  --patientId <patientId> --clinicId <clinicId>
veterical appointments update <appointmentId> --status CANCELED
veterical appointments delete <appointmentId...>    # one or more ids — permanent
```

`--status` accepts `REQUESTED`, `SCHEDULED` (the default), `CLIENT_ARRIVED`,
`NO_SHOW`, `CANCELED`. A visit the owner booked themselves on the clinic's
public site arrives as `REQUESTED` and waits for the clinic to approve it. The
window filter is start-inclusive and end-exclusive. To cancel a visit prefer
`--status CANCELED` over deleting it — deletion is permanent and also cancels
the appointment's scheduled reminders. Booking counts against the clinic's
plan; a rejected create can mean the monthly appointment allowance is used up,
not that the request was malformed.

## Invoices

```bash
veterical invoices list                             # --clinicId, --patientId
veterical invoices list --startTime <iso> --endTime <iso> -n 50 --skip 0
veterical invoices get <invoiceId>
veterical invoices read <invoiceId>
veterical invoices add --patientId <patientId> --status DRAFT --total 120 \
  --clinicId <clinicId>
veterical invoices update <invoiceId> --status PAID
veterical invoices delete <invoiceId...>            # one or more ids — permanent
```

`--status` accepts `DRAFT`, `PENDING`, `PARTIALLY_PAID`, `PAID`, `OVERDUE`,
`REFUNDED`, `UNCOLLECTIBLE`. Amounts are in the clinic currency. Line items
live in the record's own fields — send them through `--body '<json>'`.

## Payments

```bash
veterical payments list                             # --clinicId, --patientId
veterical payments list --startTime <iso> --endTime <iso> --sortField startTime
veterical payments get <paymentId>
veterical payments read <paymentId>
veterical payments add --patientId <patientId> --clinicId <clinicId> \
  --startTime <iso> --note "card terminal"
veterical payments update <paymentId> --note "corrected"
veterical payments delete <paymentId...>            # one or more ids — permanent
```

These are the clinic's own bookkeeping records. Writing one records money that
was already taken — it never charges a card, captures, refunds or moves funds.

## Vaccinations

```bash
veterical vaccinations list                         # --clinicId, --clientId
veterical vaccinations list --patientId <patientId>
veterical vaccinations list --appointmentId <appointmentId>
veterical vaccinations get <vaccinationId>
veterical vaccinations read <vaccinationId>
veterical vaccinations add --patientId <patientId> --clientId <clientId> \
  --vaccine Rabies --administeredDate 2026-07-01 --nextDueDate 2027-07-01 \
  --clinicId <clinicId>
veterical vaccinations update <vaccinationId> --nextDueDate 2027-08-01
veterical vaccinations delete <vaccinationId...>    # one or more ids — permanent
```

Vaccination records drive the clinic's recall reminders: a record carrying a
`reminders` array schedules recall jobs when written, and deleting the record
cancels them. Changing `nextDueDate` reschedules them. Do not use these records
to give medical advice or to decide what an animal should receive — they are
the clinic's log of what a veterinarian already did.

## Writes — the rules that bite

- **Every create and update needs a clinic.** An API key supplies its own
  clinic automatically; a browser session does not, so pass `--clinicId`. On
  `update` without the flag the CLI reads the record first and reuses its
  clinic — that path also needs the matching `:read` scope.
- **`update` sends only the fields you pass**, merged into the stored record.
  Arbitrary fields go through `--body '<json>'`; named options win over
  `--body` on conflict.
- **Writes fire webhooks** (`client.created`, `appointment.updated`,
  `vaccination.created`, …) to the clinic's subscribed endpoints, exactly like
  dashboard edits — a bulk import loop triggers one delivery per record.
- **Deletes are permanent** and variadic. Confirm with the user and resolve
  names to ids via `list` before deleting anything.
- These are real medical and personal records for real animals and their
  owners. Read before you write, never invent a value to satisfy a required
  flag, and never paste record contents anywhere the user did not ask for.

## Output discipline

Every subcommand accepts `--json`: real, parseable `JSON.stringify` output on
stdout — no colors, no `util.inspect`. Without the flag, `list` and `read`
print terminal summaries. Mutations with `--json` print a small result object —
`{ "ok": true, "id": "…" }` for `add`/`update`,
`{ "ok": true, "deleted": ["…"] }` for `delete`.

Failures always go to stderr with exit code 1; with `--json` the error is a
single JSON line, `{"error":{"message":"…","status":404}}`, so stdout stays
parseable.

When exploring, project instead of dumping — use `--fields` server-side or pipe
`--json` through `jq` and keep only what you need:

```bash
veterical clients list --json --fields _id,name,email | jq '.[] | {id: ._id, name}'
```

## Configuration

`VETERICAL_API_URL` overrides the API endpoint (default
`https://api.veterical.com`) — only for non-production deployments.
`VETERICAL_API_KEY` supplies an API key secret from the environment for
headless use — no login step needed, but a stored login outranks it. Stored
credentials live only in `~/.veterical/`.

## Errors → remediation

| Symptom                                 | Fix                                                   |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `401` / "Not logged in?"                | `veterical login`, or export `VETERICAL_API_KEY`, then retry |
| `403: Invalid api key`                  | The stored secret is wrong — `veterical login --with-key` again |
| `403` naming a missing scope            | Widen the key's scopes in the Veterical dashboard     |
| `404` on an id you were given           | Wrong id, or the record belongs to another clinic     |
| `400: missing clinicId`                 | Pass `--clinicId` (see Writes above)                  |
| `429`                                   | Per-key rate limit — wait, do not retry-loop          |
| An owner appears twice                  | `add` is not idempotent — list by `--email` first     |
